reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text:
Hi @clairlemon. I've been thinking about the possibility of 'conscious AI' since 2009 (https://t.co/VCtZaYIrXJ). I am a vocal skeptic, but I don't think it helps to characterise those who think AI might be conscious as 'insane'. Polarisation is dangerous, and the question of 'AI consciousness' is scientific, not political. There are good arguments on both side. IMO the sceptical arguments are far stronger, but others disagree & I respect and engage with their views. 

For a representative take on the state of the debate in academia, see this just-published @BBSJournal collection, which has my target article, 50 peer commentaries, and my response.  https://t.co/pzszCvMSgB
reviewedPosts.rationale: 研究出版信息，技术证据有限

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text: Indeed. I’ve a lot of respect for my colleagues in philosophy, neuroscience, and AI who are more open to the possibility of AI consciousness, and who make their case rationally. I still think they're wrong. But the issue is so important that it is a disservice to dismiss either side as deluded. https://t.co/vDvw82ookk

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
好奇大家现在还会线下看脱口秀吗？

昨天和一个在杭州全职做脱口秀的同学吃饭，聊了不少行业里的事。

他说现在写段子、上台都得特别小心。像躺平、就业压力、男女对立这些题材，只要稍微沾边，演出前就可能被要求修改。演员录播客也一样，一些敏感内容最后会直接被 B 掉。

听完还是挺感慨的。

脱口秀好玩的地方，本来就是把很多大家心里有、平时又不太会直接说的东西以一种调侃方式讲出来。如果能聊的东西越来越少，最后最难的可能不是怎么把段子写好，而是还能不能讲出点真实的东西。

当然，这只是我同学作为从业者的一线体感，我也就是吃饭时听来的转述😂
